## Source and sample

The clinical illustration uses `IBScovars` from **DoseFinding 1.4-1**.
The source is the [CRAN package archive](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DoseFinding).
The analysis retained all **369 released observations**, with dose counts
71, 78, 75, 72, and 73 at codes 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. No observation was excluded,
imputed, standardized, or transformed for this analysis. The released outcome
is a baseline-adjusted abdominal-pain response score; larger values indicate
greater improvement according to the source documentation.

The release contains completers, so this is not an intention-to-treat
reconstruction. Active physical doses and spacing are not supplied. The
equal-spacing code convention is explicit and affects the integrated target.

## Bundled aggregate files

`clinical_dose_summary.tsv` contains dose-level summaries derived from the
unchanged released sample. `clinical_intervals.tsv` contains the saved
completed interval results. The package contains no individual-level clinical
data.

```{r dictionary, echo=FALSE}
dictionary <- data.frame(
  File = c(rep("Dose summary", 4), rep("Interval results", 5)),
  Field = c("dose", "n", "mean", "sd", "method / label", "status", "estimate / qhat", "lower / upper / width", "calibration"),
  Meaning = c("Ordered dose code, 0 through 4; not a physical dose",
    "Number of released observations at that dose",
    "Sample mean of the released response",
    "Sample standard deviation with denominator n - 1",
    "Recorded method identifier and display label",
    "Recorded numerical status",
    "Common fitted target estimate and shape estimate",
    "Reported interval endpoints and width in response units",
    "Description of the method's calibration"))
knitr::kable(dictionary)
```

## Pooled variance

Let $s_j$ be the dose-specific sample standard deviation and $n_j$ its count.
The pooled within-dose variance for $m$ dose levels is computed as

$$S^2=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^m(n_j-1)s_j^2}{\sum_{j=1}^m n_j-m}.$$

This expression pools pure error under the common-variance assumption; its
denominator is the pure-error degrees of freedom. It reproduces the variance
used by the confidence region, up to the precision of the saved summary text.
It is not estimated from deviations about a fitted Emax curve.

## Reuse and publication status

The source package and aggregate summaries are available from the package
website and GitHub repository. Source-dataset documentation
and applicable reuse conditions should accompany any future deposition.
